title: Decentralized IaC CI: per-environment plan signing, OPA soft-fail policy advisor, and post-apply health prober
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement a CI workflow for Private (VPC) Terraform that: (1) produces signed plan artifacts per environment to prevent unsigned/modified plans being applied, (2) runs an OPA/Conftest policy advisor in a non-blocking advisory mode for developer guidance, and (3) executes a post-apply health prober that validates runtime invariants and surfaces auto-rollback triggers. This aims to reduce drift, make plan reviews cryptographically verifiable, and detect regressions within the first 10 minutes after apply.
acceptance_criteria: CI generates a terraform plan artifact (.tfplan) for each environment and stores it in the artifact bucket with metadata (env, workspace, git-commit, pipeline-run).
Each plan artifact is signed using sigstore/cosign with a short-lived key linked to the pipeline identity and the signature is verifiable by a separate apply runner service.

OPA/Conftest policy advisor runs against plan and returns categorized findings: FAIL (block only for security-critical rules), ADVISE (soft-fail, shown prominently in PR and pipeline output), and IGNORE. Advisories include example remediation hints and links to policy docs.
Apply jobs refuse unsigned or tampered plan artifacts; tamper attempts are logged and create an incident with evidence bundle.

Post-apply health prober runs smoke checks (VPC connectivity, DNS resolution, service port checks, IAM sanity, basic e2e scenario) within 5-10 minutes; failures mark the build and initiate configured rollback policy or alert channel depending on severity.
Documentation and runbook created: how to interpret OPA advisories, how to escalate health-prober failures, and steps to re-run plan signing if needed.
Automated tests for signing/verification and the advisor behavior exist in the pipeline unit test job.
Updated RBAC ensures only pipeline service principals with cosign signing privileges can sign plans; keys are provisioned via KMS/HSM and rotated every 30 days.
implementation_notes: Plan signing approach: use Sigstore/cosign to sign plan blobs. Pipeline runner obtains short-lived signing token via KMS-bound OIDC flow; avoids long-lived private keys in CI. Verification performed by the apply-runner using public transparency logs.

Artifact storage: plans uploaded to s3://redwood-iac-plans/<env>/<workspace>/<run-id>/<commit>.tfplan, server-side encrypted (SSE-KMS). Signed payload includes env, git commit, workspace, and pipeline run id as annotations.

OPA/Conftest setup: keep rules minimal for first rollouts. Security-critical policies enforced as hard-fails (e.g., public S3, unrestricted SG egress), cost/ops policies are ADVISE by default (e.g., large instance types). Provide a centralized policy repo (policies/opa and policies/conftest) and an 'advisor' wrapper that formats findings into PR comments and pipeline annotations.

Apply runner: separate ephemeral runner with least privilege applies artifacts after verifying signature. Runner supports canary apply flag (percent of resources or subset of stacks) and automatic rollback via stored state snapshots.

Health-prober details: lightweight Go binary that runs a sequence of checks configured per environment. Built checks: TCP check, DNS resolution, IAM permission test (read-only list), sample API request (if service exposes a health endpoint). Results posted to pipeline and to monitoring (Datadog) with tags pipeline_run, env, commit.

Failure handling: define severity mapping in config: critical => immediate rollback and paging, warning => ticket and slack incident channel. Rollback uses latest known-good state snapshot stored encrypted in artifact store.
Gradual rollout: start on dev/staging workspaces, run advisory mode for prod for 2 cycles, then flip blocking rules for critical security policies. Track false positives and iterate on policies.
Metrics to add: plan-sign success rate, advisor advisory-to-fix time, apply rollback frequency after health-prober, mean time to detect post-apply regressions.
Local dev experience: provide 'iac-cli verify-plan --file myplan.tfplan' to validate signature and run advisor locally so engineers can iterate without pushing PRs.
progress_updates: 2025-02-08: Kickoff meeting with infra, security, and platform; scoped features and owners. Decided on sigstore/cosign for signing to avoid self-managed private key storage.
2025-02-11: Prototype: pipeline job creates tfplan, uploads to S3, and signed successfully with cosign in OIDC flow. Uploaded sample to dev bucket. Logged prototype artifacts in test account.
2025-02-13: OPA policy initial set drafted. Security rules reviewed by Security team; three rules marked hard-fail candidates: public S3 buckets, SG 0.0.0.0/0, and unmanaged KMS keys.
2025-02-15: Built advisor wrapper that massages Conftest output into GitHub PR comments and a summarized table for pipeline UI. First PR comment format approved by DX team.
2025-02-18: Started implementation of apply-runner verification flow. Implemented verification step that fetches S3 artifact and validates cosign signature, with annotations for env/workspace.

2025-02-20: Health-prober PoC completed for staging: TCP/DNS/health-endpoint checks run in pipeline; one false positive identified due to DNS TTL; adjusted retry logic. Preparing rollout plan for dev->staging.
